meta.title: CMBS Distress Monitor
meta.history_policy: Only verified public prints. Missing months are omitted, not interpolated.
meta.as_of_note: Newest verified observation period in the file is October 2026 (CRED iQ distress). Trepp series last verified September 2026. Not the compile date.

trepp_overall.name: Trepp US CMBS delinquency (30+ days)
trepp_overall.notes: Headline Trepp CMBS delinquency rate. Performing matured balloons are excluded from the headline rate.

trepp_serious.notes: Seriously delinquent rate as defined by Trepp.

trepp_performing_balloon.notes: Loans past maturity date but current on interest. Separate from headline delinquency.

crediq_distress.name: CRED iQ conduit and SASB distress (delinquent, past maturity, or special servicing)
crediq_distress.notes: Distress defined as balance 30+ days delinquent, past maturity (performing or not), or in special servicing. Conduit and SASB only.

conclusions: Stock: Trepp 30+ delinquency was 8.02 percent (up 17 bp), serious delinquency 7.87 percent (up 18 bp), and special servicing 11.49 percent (up 7 bp) in September 2026; performing matured balloon was 1.64 percent. CRED iQ distress rate was 11.2 percent in October 2026 for conduit and SASB.
Flow: Five large single-asset single-borrower loans drove much of the September delinquency increase; non-performing matured balloons accounted for 68 percent of newly delinquent balances.
Wall: Including performing matured balloons, the Trepp rate was 9.66 percent in September, down 15 bp from August.
withheld: No conclusion: Trepp October delinquency and special servicing last verified none (no public print released as of this run).
No conclusion: MBA Commercial Delinquency Report Q3 last verified none (different survey series verified instead).

events.detail: Five largest newly delinquent loans: $1.10 billion eight-property studio-and-office portfolio in Los Angeles, $470.0 million two-tower office complex in Houston, $280.0 million beachfront hotel in Santa Monica, $230.1 million office in Denver, $208.9 million single-tenant office in Silicon Valley. Non-performing matured balloon loans accounted for 68 percent of newly delinquent balances.

CRED iQ property alerts flagged $4.5 billion of conduit and SASB CMBS debt as newly delinquent or newly in special servicing in October, 93 percent of it past maturity or within six months of it. Office $1.5 billion, hotels $1.1 billion, retail $0.7 billion, industrial $0.5 billion.
events.source: CRED iQ Blog, CMBS Distress Shifts Away From New York, October 29, 2026

ratings.detail: Reviewed 44 North American CMBS deals. Actions on 470 classes: 355 confirmations, 93 downgrades, 13 upgrades, 9 Under Review Negative. Downgrades driven by higher projected losses on specially serviced loans and underperforming assets, with office properties driving significant pressure.
ratings.document: Monthly North American CMBS Rating Action Summary: September 2026

ratings.detail: Delinquency rate for loans packaged in U.S. CMBS transactions dropped to 8.74 percent in September 2026, a decrease of 13 basis points from August 2026.
